text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms of a pontine stroke can include muscle weakness on one side of the body, facial weakness or drooping, abnormal sensations, slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, and balance issues. Other potential symptoms include vertigo, double vision, and decreased consciousness. Pontine strokes can also cause paralysis, ataxia (loss of coordination), and locked-in syndrome in severe cases.
snippet_highlighted_words: muscle weakness on one side of the body, facial weakness or drooping, abnormal sensations, slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, and balance issues

list.snippet: Weakness or paralysis: This can affect one side of the body (hemiparesis) or both arms and legs (quadriplegia).
Facial weakness: Drooping on one or both sides of the face is a common sign.
Loss of coordination or balance: This can manifest as ataxia.
Abnormal sensations: Numbness, tingling, or pain on one side of the face or body.
